correctness.rationale: PASS: For m=3^a, separate the alternating C_(2m) cotangent block into m-th roots of unity !=1 and roots eta^m=-1. Galois invariance gives rationality; denominators 1-xi for primitive 3^j roots have norm 3 and are integral away from 3, while eta roots yield units away from the lone trivial eta=-1 zero. For primitive cube roots the 3-adic valuation of u(xi)^(2m) equals -m and their combined term is 2(-1/3)^m with unit coefficient; all primitive 3^j,j>=2 terms have valuation >=-m/3 and the odd block is integral. Thus C_(2m) has exact v3=-m and normalized numerator 1 mod3. In the original Agustín-Aquino affine-divisor theorem specialized to n=2*3^a, the top block has coefficient one and all lower blocks coefficients 2*3^(2(a-j)-1), valuations strictly greater than -3^a. They cannot cancel the unique leading term, proving all a. Independent exact Newton-sum computations for a=1,2,3 yielded denominators 27,19683,7625597484987, each numerator 1 mod3; bounded tests corroborate the p-adic argument.
